title: Stephen Miller's unhinged rant on 'fighting politically correct' and 'woke Pentagon' - NewsBreak
text:
By Ananya Chetia ,
1 hours ago Homeland Security Advisor Stephen Miller went on Fox News Wednesday night and said the military is "not fighting politically correct" and called the previous administration a "woke Pentagon."
Miller spoke to Fox News television presenter Sean Hannity on Wednesday about why the Trump administration struck Iran on Feb. 28, which also killed Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khomeini and his family members. Hannity said he believed Trump is "America first."
"You know, I am tired of the absolute ignorance of some people in the punditry class and Democratic Party, whoever it happens to be. 'Oh, Donald Trump did this on behalf of Bibi Netanyahu., Donald Trump does not do anything based on what anybody asks,'" Hannity said.
• AOC says Trump willing to plunge US into WW3 to 'save himself from Epstein files'
• Two more US soldiers killed in Iran war identified as tragic human cost increases
"He is a man that knows his own mind and his agenda, and he is America first," the television presenter added.
Miller said Trump's move to strike Iran was "to protect and defend America's interests, not to surrender the world to our adversaries."
"What you're seeing right now, Sean, is a military under President Trump's leadership that's not fighting politically correct, that isn't fighting with its hands tied behind its back," he said.
Miller added Iran's regime of 47 years bombed U.S marines in Beirut and kidnapped, tortured and murdered the CIA station chief.
"One of the reasons I fear, Sean, that some people in this country lost faith in the military and the capacity to use that military to defend us is because we had a woke Pentagon, because we had a military who, at the very highest levels, not the war fighters, was forced to fight a less than full fight. What you're seeing now, Sean, is a military that is unleashed in all of its lethal prowess to go out and seek, destroy and kill the enemy, which is what militaries are for."
Iran began attacking Gulf nations with drone strikes after the U.S and Israel first struck the country on Feb.28. Along with Ayatollah Khomeini being killed, the U.S- and Israel-led strikes also destroyed a school and killed 165 people.
The majority of the victims were girls aged between 7 and 12, Iranian authorities said. At least 95 people were also wounded in the attack.
On Monday, the U.S. Department of State requested Americans to depart over a dozen countries in the Middle East.
Such countries include Bahrain, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Israel, the occupied West Bank and Gaza, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Syria, the United Arab Emirates and Yemen.
The war on Iran led to the death of six U.S military members. Their identities were released on Tuesday.
Capt. Cody A. Khork, 35, of Winter Haven, Florida; Sgt. 1st Class Noah L. Tietjens, 42, of Bellevue, Nebraska; Sgt. 1st Class Nicole M. Amor, 39, of White Bear Lake, Minnesota; and Sgt. Declan J. Coady, 20, of West Des Moines, Iowa were four out of the six who died on Saturday from an Iranian drone strike.
